items.text: For two weeks across France, people have been protesting and making public demonstrations. The Cilet Jaunes (‘Yellow Vests’) started as a fuel tax protest, but now authorities say that far-right extremists are co-opting them. Authorities are also condemning the spread and the violence of all of these protests. This weekend, a march of 17,000 climate protesters peacefully walked through Paris, but after the march, smaller groups of protesters began to riot . Some wore yellow vests. Police arrested hundreds of protesters after they destroyed a sports shop at the Place de la Republique. Difficult words: far-right extremist (a person who wants a government to support only its people and thinks that they are superior people who should rule other people), co-op t (adopt someone else’s idea for your use), condemn (say that you really do not like something), riot (throw and break things in the streets and attack people). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In France, people have been protesting and demonstrating for two weeks. The main protest started against a fuel tax , but now authorities say that far-right extremists are taking over the protests to spread their ideas. Authorities also do not like the amount and the violence of the protests. This weekend, a march of 17,000 climate protesters peacefully walked in Paris, but afterwards, some protesters began to riot . Police arrested hundreds of protesters after they destroyed a shop. Difficult words: fuel tax (extra money you must pay to the government when you buy gas or coal), far-right extremist (a person who wants a government to support only its people and thinks that they are better people than other people), riot (throw and break things in the streets and attack people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In France, people are angry. They protest against a fuel tax . They protest for two weeks. Authorities do not like the violence of the protests. They do not like that so many protests are happening. They say that some extremists are taking over the protests. This weekend, 17,000 protesters peacefully walk in Paris. Afterwards, some protesters riot . They destroy a shop. Police arrest hundreds of them. Difficult words: fuel tax (extra money that you have to pay for fuel, gas or coal for example), violence (throwing and breaking of things and attacking people), extremist (a person with very strong views), riot (throw and break things in the streets and attack people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At Oakland Zoo in California, USA, Mousa is a newborn Hamadryas baboon; he is one month old and mainly clings onto his mum, Mocha. The animals come from the Horn of Africa . The zoo says that the Hamadryas baboon population is overall increasing. Difficult words: cling (hold onto very tightly), Horn of Africa (the north-eastern part of Africa that is shaped like a horn). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At Oakland Zoo in California, USA, a baby baboon was born. He is one month old now and spends his time with his mum, as he clings onto her. These baboons come from the north-east of Africa. The zoo says that their population is increasing . Difficult words: cling (hold onto tightly), population (the number of living things), increase (get more). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Oakland Zoo is in California, USA. A baby baboon is born there. He is one month old now. He spends all of his time with his mum. He clings onto her. These baboons are from the north-east of Africa. The zoo says that their population is going up. Difficult words: baboon (a monkey that lives on the ground), cling (hold onto), population (the number of animals or people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The National Rifle Association (NRA) is an American organisation that advocates for gun rights. In one of its adverts, it used an image of the famous sculpture ’The Bean’ by the British sculptor Anish Kapoor. Kapoor was ‘disgusted’ that his art was associated with ‘a campaign of fear and hate’, and he wanted his work removed from the ad named ‘The Clenched Fist of Truth’. After the NRA failed to remove the image, Kapoor launched a copyright lawsuit . In the end, the issue was settled out of court and the image was removed from the video. The artist said that the victory was ‘a declaration that we stand with those who oppose gun violence’. Difficult words: advocate (speak for), clenched (closed tightly), fist (the way you close your hand when you want to hit somebody), copyright lawsuit (when you sue for someone using your ideas without permission), declaration (a statement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The National Rifle Association (NRA) is an American organisation which is for gun rights. In one of its adverts, it used an image of the famous sculpture ’The Bean’. The creator of ‘The Bean’, the British sculptor Anish Kapoor, was ‘disgusted’ that his art was used in ‘a campaign of fear and hate’. He wanted the NRA to remove the image, and the NRA did not remove the image right away, but did so eventually . The artist said that the victory was ‘a declaration that we stand with those who oppose gun violence’. Difficult words: sculpture (a three dimensional piece of art), eventually (in the end), declaration (a statement). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The NRA is an American organisation. It is for gun rights . This organisation runs TV ads . In one of its ads, there is an image of a famous sculpture . The sculpture is ‘The Bean’. It is by the British artist Anish Kapoor. He is disgusted that his art is in an ad for guns. He wants the NRA not to use his image. The NRA does not want to do this. However, in the end, it stops using the picture. Difficult words: gun rights (the idea that people can have and carry guns), ad (a commercial for something), sculpture (art that is an object), disgusted (angry, the opposite of happy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Heavy rain and hailstorms hit parts of Saudi Arabia recently – this was extreme weather for the desert country. The storms hit one provincial capital particularly hard and its streets were submerged with what appeared to be a strange sludge but was actually icy flash flood water. Difficult words: hailstorm (a storm of hail – frozen rain), submerge (get under water), sludge (a mixture of snow, mud and water), flash flood (a sudden, local flood caused by heavy rain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Recently heavy rain and hailstorms hit parts of Saudi Arabia, and the streets of one city were completely under water. From a video, it looks like sludge , but it is icy water. Difficult words: hailstorm (a storm of hail – frozen rain), sludge (a mixture of snow, mud and water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Saudi Arabia is a desert country. Rain and hail are extreme weather there. Heavy rain and hailstorms hit. The streets of one city go completely under water. Somebody films the streets. The streets look like sludge . However, they are icy water. Difficult words: desert (a very dry area with sand or rocks), extreme (very strong), hail (frozen rain), sludge (a mixture of snow, mud and water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Spanish royal family celebrated 40 years since the Spanish Constitution which over 90 per cent of the population approved in the 1978 referendum . In a speech in the Spanish parliament, King Felipe VI said that modern Spain should be proud of the constitution. Meanwhile, protesters took to the streets in an anti-monarchy demonstration – some people there think that the monarchy no longer represents the needs of the working class. Difficult words: Constitution (the basic ideas and laws of a government that tells about its powers and its people’s rights), referendum (when the people of a country choose changes to happen in that country), demonstration (a formal protest). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Spanish royal family celebrated 40 years since the Spanish Constitution that was approved in a referendum in 1978. Over 90 per cent of people were for it. King Felipe VI gave a speech in the Spanish parliament, and he said that modern Spain should be proud of the constitution. Meanwhile, some people protested against the monarchy . They think that the monarchy no longer represents the needs of the working class. Difficult words: Constitution (a document that explains the laws and ideas of a country), approve (say ‘yes’ to something), referendum (when people vote on something), monarchy (the form of government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

December 6th is Constitution Day in Spain. This year, the Spanish constitution is 40 years old. In 1978, there was a referendum . Over 90% of the people wanted the constitution. Now, some people do not want the constitution. They protest. They think that it is not good for working class people . Difficult words: Constitution (a document that tells about the laws and ideas of a country), was (past of ‘is’), referendum (when people can say if they want something to happen in their country), working class people (people who work but do not have a lot of money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There was a stampede in an Italian nightclub after someone sprayed a noxious substance similar to pepper spray. Six people died (including five teenagers and a 39-year-old mother accompanying her daughter) and 50 more were injured in the incident which happened early on Saturday morning near Italy’s central Adriatic coast. Difficult words: stampede (when many people get scared and start running), noxious (nasty, very unpleasant), substance (a gas or a liquid), accompany (go somewhere with someone). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Somebody sprayed a substance similar to pepper spray at a nightclub in Italy which made people panic , and there was a stampede . Six people died in the stampede and 50 more were injured. Five of the killed were teenagers. The incident happened early on Saturday morning. Difficult words: substance (gas or liquid), panic (when you get so scared you start to run away without thinking), stampede (when many people get scared and start running). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from a nightclub in Italy. Somebody sprays something like pepper spray . People start to panic . They start running. There is a stampede . Six people die in the stampede. Five of them are teenagers. Fifty more people are injured. This happened early on Saturday morning. Difficult words: panic (when you get so scared that you cannot think), pepper spray (a spray which hurts your eyes – police use it to get people to stop doing something), stampede (when many people get scared and start running), happened (past of ‘happen’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Italian authorities released footage of daring night time raids to dismantle the Sicilian Mafia. The police used cover surveillance and wiretaps to monitor multiple suspects who they suspect of Mafia association, extortion and weapons violations. In total, they arrested 46 people, including a presumed new regional boss. Difficult words: daring (brave), raid (surprise attack), dismantle (break), surveillance (spying), wiretap (listening to somebody secretly), suspect (somebody who the police think is a criminal), extortion (forcing someone to give you money), presumed (believed to be). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Italian police released videos of raids to break up the Sicilian Mafia. They spied on people who they suspected of various crimes. They arrested forty-six people in total. Difficult words: raid (a surprise or sneak attack), suspected (thought to be guilty of a crime), various (different types of). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Sicily is in Italy. The Sicilian Mafia is there. The Sicilian police fight the Mafia. The police monitors people. The police releases videos of raids . They arrest 46 people. Difficult words: Mafia (an organised crime group that comes from Italy), monitor (watch), release (show to everyone), raid (a surprise attack). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe’s most expensive Christmas tree, which is made of 63 kilogrammes of gold coins, has gone on display in Munich, Germany. It stands at nearly three metres tall and is worth 2.3 million Euros. Difficult words: worth (have value in money) You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Europe’s most expensive Christmas tree is in Munich, Germany, and it is made of 63 kilogrammes of gold coins. It is three metres tall, it is under 24-hour surveillance , and it is worth 2.3 million Euros. Difficult words: surveillance (watching for security), worth (have value in money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about an expensive Christmas tree. It is in Munich, Germany. It is made of 63 kilogrammes of gold coins . It is three metres tall. It is Europe’s most expensive Christmas tree. It is worth 2.3 million Euros. Security watches it 24/7 . Difficult words: coins (round metal circles which people use as money), worth (have a price in money), 24/7 (all of the time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People called George H. W. Bush the ‘ odd job ’ man in politics, as he undertook short notice and difficult tasks throughout his life. Prior to politics, Bush was the youngest Naval aviator in WWII in Navy history, and he became a millionaire running an oil company. Then he entered politics in Houston, Texas, and he worked in different positions to keep the people working there united and to restore morale . In 1980, Ronald Regan brought Bush on as vice president, and in 1989, the American people elected him as the 41 st president of the US. He had a busy beginning with many events happening, but he handled them all. In 1992, Bush lost the re-election to Democrat Bill Clinton. Later on, Bush saw his son become the 43 rd president. Until his death this year, Bush was the oldest living US president. Difficult words: odd job (an unusual job or task), undertook (work on something difficult), aviator (a pilot of a plane), restore morale (help a group of people feel better about a situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People called George H. W. Bush the ‘ odd job ’ man in politics because he took short notice and difficult tasks. Before politics, Bush was a WWII pilot and then he became a millionaire running an oil company. When he entered politics, he worked in different positions to keep the people working there united and to restore morale . In 1980, Bush was vice president with Ronald Regan, and in 1989, the American people elected him as the 41 st president. Later on, Bush’s son become the 43 rd president. Until his death this year, Bush was the oldest living US president. Difficult words: odd job (a strange job or thing to do), short notice (when you do not have a lot of time to work on something), restore morale (help a group of people feel better about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

George H. W. Bush is one of the US presidents. Before he is president, he flies planes in WWII. He makes a lot of money running an oil company. He works in politics . He helps people feel better about their jobs. In 1980, Bush is vice -president to Ronald Reagan. In 1989, the American people elect Bush as president. Later, his son is also president. Bush is the oldest living US president. He dies this year. Difficult words: politics (the running of a government), vice- (a job that helps another person with his or her job), elect (choose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

While the Pope spoke at the Vatican, a six-year old boy named Wenzel came on stage to play, but Pope Francis told his guards to let the boy stay. The boy is mute and could not easily respond to them. The Pope replied to the audience that though Wenzel could not speak, ‘he does know how to express himself’ and ‘he is free’. His mother eventually took him off-stage, but he had already captured everyone’s hearts . The Pope ended his catechism lesson with a prayer for Wenzel. Difficult words: mute (a person who is unable to speak with his or her voice), capture hearts (make someone else feel love), catechism (a summary of important parts of Christianity in questions and answers to teach Christians). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

While the Pope spoke at the Vatican, a six-year old boy came on stage to play, and Pope Francis told his guards to let the boy stay. The boy is mute and could not easily respond. The Pope spoke to the audience that though the boy was unable to speak, he was able ‘to express himself’ and ‘he is free’. His mother later took him off-stage, but he had already captured everyone’s hearts . The Pope ended his speech with a prayer for the boy. Difficult words: mute (a person who cannot speak with his or her voice), express (communicate), capture hearts (make another person feel love). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Pope is speaking at the Vatican. A six-year old boy comes on the stage with him. He wants to play. The Pope tells his guards that it is OK. The boy is mute . The Pope talks about the boy. He says that the boy cannot speak. However, the boy can ‘ express himself ’. He says that the boy ‘is free ’. The boy’s mother takes him off of the stage. Everyone loves the little boy. The Pope prays for him. Difficult words: stage (an area where speakers/actors are), mute (a person who cannot speak), express oneself (tell how you feel or think through your words or your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Another NASA probe successfully landed on Mars. It took it six months to travel the 480-million-kilometre journey and before touchdown, it had to slow down from its speed of 19,000 kilometres per hour. Friction and drag during the descent through the upper Martian atmosphere began the initial slowdown, and before the rocket thrusters slowly landed the probe, a parachute brought it to a more manageable speed. The landing sequence took just six minutes and it was fully automated. People at NASA were delighted after their creation sent them a selfie. The probe will be the first one to drill below the surface of the red planet. A so-called mole will be burrowed five metres down to measure the planet’s internal heat and a seismometer will listen for any “marsquakes”. Difficult words: probe (an unmanned spacecraft), friction (the force which slows down an aircraft – it happens when air hits the aircraft), drag (a force which slows down aircraft), descent (the act of moving down), mole (a small black animal which lives underground), burrow (go under the ground), seismometer ( a seismograph – a device which measures earthquakes). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA sent a probe to Mars that travelled 480-million-kilometres over six months. Before landing, it had to slow down from its speed of 19,000 kilometres per hour. After it landed, it sent people at NASA a selfie. The probe will be the first one to drill below the surface of the red planet . It will put sensors five metres below the ground to measure the planet’s internal heat, and a seismometer will listen for any “marsquakes”. Difficult words: probe (an unmanned spacecraft), the red planet (a nickname for Mars because its ground is red), seismometer (a measuring device that measures earthquakes – when the ground moves). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA sends a probe to Mars. It travels 480 million kilometres. The journey takes six months. It travels at 19,000 kilometres per hour. The probe lands safely. After the landing, it sends people a selfie. The probe is the first probe to drill into the ground of Mars. It goes five metres below the ground. It measures the temperature. It measures earthquakes, too. Difficult words: probe (a machine which people send to space), journey (way), drill (make a hole, make a space in the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People transformed Edinburgh Zoo in Scotland with giant lanterns of mythical creatures from Scottish and Chinese folklore. Unicorns , mythical birds, dragons and dinosaurs took 200 artisans from China more than three months to create. The result is over 450 hand-crafted lanterns forming a magical trail through the zoo. The trail uses 50,000 metres of fabric and 80,000 LED lights, and the exhibit’s aim is to illuminate the crucial conservation work that the zoo undertakes . Difficult words: lantern (a model made of paper or fabric with lights inside), unicorn (a mythical animal which looks like a horse with a horn), artisan (a skilled worker who makes things by hand), crucial (very important), undertake (tackle, work on something difficult). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People transformed Edinburgh Zoo in Scotland into a magical place with more than 450 lanterns of mythical animals from Scottish and Chinese folklore. Unicorns , mythical birds, dragons and dinosaurs took 200 artisans from China more than three months to create. They used around 50,000 metres of fabric and 80,000 LED lights. Difficult words: lantern (a model made of paper or fabric with lights inside), unicorn (a mythical animal which looks like a horse with a horn), artisan (a skilled worker who makes things by hand). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a zoo in Edinburgh, Scotland. This winter, there is a magical exhibit at the zoo. There are 450 lanterns . The lanterns look like mythical animals. The animals are from Scottish and Chinese stories and traditions. Two hundred people from China work on the exhibit. It takes them three months. They use 50,000 metres of fabric. They also use 80,000 lights. Difficult words: exhibit (an art show), lantern (a model made of paper or fabric with lights inside), mythical (from old stories). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The American President Trump, the Canadian President Justin Trudeau and the former (since December) President of Mexico, Peña Nieto, signed a new US-Mexico-Canada trade agreement. The signing of the agreement took place at the G20 in Buenos Aires, Argentina, but it was mostly ceremonial, as the agreement still needs to be approved and put into practice by all countries before it takes effect. It replaces NAFTA which the countries signed in 1994. Difficult words: former (-ex), NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The American, Canadian and Mexican presidents signed a new trade agreement . The signing took place at the G20 summit in Buenos Aires Argentina, and the new agreement replaces NAFTA which the countries signed in 1994. Difficult words: agreement (a deal, a plan to do something), summit (a meeting between leaders of countries), replace (take place of something else). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NAFTA is an agreement . It is an agreement between the USA, Canada and Mexico. It is an agreement about free trade between these three countries. NAFTA is old. It is from 1994. The American, Canadian and Mexican presidents sign a new agreement. They sign it in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Difficult words: agreement (a plan to do something), trade (buying and selling things), sign (write down your name to show that you say ‘yes’ to something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Christmas arrived at the White House and the First Lady Melania Trump has been the designer of this and last year’s Christmas decor. The official name of this year’s Christmas theme is ‘American Treasures ’ which features the skylines of several major American cities. Not all of the decorations are to everyone’s liking though – some people commented on a corridor decorated with red trees. They thought that it conveyed feelings of horror and compared it with a scene from the horror film ’The Shining’. To others, it looked like the robes from the dystopian TV show ‘The Handmaid’s Tale’. Last year, many people found Melania’s theme spooky and eerie rather than festive. Difficult words: theme (the way something looks), treasure (something very important and loved), convey (carry, communicate), dystopian (a negative story about the future), spooky (frightening, scary), eerie (strange and scary). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Christmas has arrived at the White House, and it was Melania Trump who designed this and last year’s Christmas decor. The official name of this year’s Christmas theme is ‘American Treasures ’, and it features the skylines of some American cities. Some people like the decorations, and some people do not. Online, some people commented about a corridor decorated with red leave. They thought that it looked like a scene from a scary movie. Some people did not like the 2017 decorations, either. They thought that they looked scary and not Christmas-y . Difficult words: theme (the way something looks or the ideas about it), treasure (something very important and loved), feature (have), -y (this ending can turn a noun into adjective; Christmas-y means that something should like Christmas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Christmas is coming. Melania Trump decorates the White House. The decorations are about Christmas. They are also about American treasures . For example, there are skylines of some cities. Some people like the decorations. Some people do not. There are some red Christmas trees. Some people think that they look like blood. They do not like them. They think that they look like they are from a horror film. Difficult words: decorate (make pretty), treasure (something very important and loved), skyline (a picture of a city’s famous buildings). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Following months of growing tensions between Russia and Ukraine, a video shows the moment that a Ukrainian boat and a Russian coast guard vessel collided off the coast of Crimea. There were in total three Ukrainian vessels sailing in the sea when the incident happened. Russia said that they made an unauthorised passage through Russian territorial waters, and the Russian boat later opened fire on the vessels before seizing them. Ukrainian authorities, on the other hand, said that their boats did nothing wrong and accused Russia of military aggression. Difficult words: tensions (problems, negative feelings), coast guard (the people who protect the coast of a country), collide (crash into), vessel (a boat), seize (formally capture or take). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There are growing tensions between Russia and Ukraine and a recent incident made matters worse. There were three Ukrainian boats and a Russian boat that were sailing in the Black Sea when the Russian boat hit one of the Ukrainian boats. Later it fired on the boats, and the Russians seized them. Russia said that the Ukrainian boats were in their waters. Ukraine said that the boats did nothing wrong and that Russia was aggressive. Difficult words: tensions (problems, bad feelings), incident (a memorable event), matters (a situation, things), seize (capture, take). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are tensions between Russia and Ukraine. An incident at sea makes the situation worse. There are four boats. Three are Ukrainian. One is Russian. The Russian boat hits one of the Ukrainian boats. The Russian boat also fires on the Ukrainian boats. Russian men then seize the other boats. Russia says that the Ukrainian boats are in Russian waters. Ukraine says that the boats did nothing bad. Ukraine says that Russia is aggressive . Difficult words: tensions (problems), fire (shoot), seize (take), aggressive (wanting to fight). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In May in the United Arab Emirates, a court convicted 31-year-old Matthew Hedges, a British Ph.D. student, to a 25-year sentence for spying. Hedges contested that he was there to study for his degree. A British government official said that at the hearing , Hedges was not allowed to have his lawyer, the hearing took five minutes, and the British media was banned. The verdict shocked his family and the UK government. Officials questioned their ties to the country, with one asking why they should want to defend the UAE if Hedges was kept in jail in these circumstances. The UAE’s king recently decided to release Hedges among another 785 prisoners due to his family’s request for clemency and ‘in consideration to the close ties and historical relationship’ between the two countries. Difficult words: convict (find someone is guilty of a crime), contest (argue against someone), hearing (a legal proceeding), verdict (a decision on if someone is innocent or guilty of a crime), tie (a relationship), clemency (mercy), consideration (thinking a lot about something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In May in the United Arab Emirates, a court found that a British student was guilty of spying and sent him to jail for 25 years. A British government official said that at the hearing , the student could not have his lawyer, it took five minutes, and the British media was banned . The decision shocked the student’s family and the UK government, and some officials questioned why they should work with the country. Recently, the UAE’s king decided to release the student with other prisoners because of his family’s request for clemency and the historical relationship between the two countries. Difficult words: hearing (a legal event where you can talk about if you are innocent or guilty of a crime), ban (to not allow somebody something), clemency (forgiving someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A British student goes to the United Arab Emirates to study. In May, a court has a hearing with this student. People think that he is a spy. The student does not have his lawyer there. People say that the hearing is fast. They say that the British media cannot be there. The court says that he is guilty . It sends him to jail. This shocks the student’s family. It shocks the UK government . Suddenly, the UAE’s king lets prisoners free. The student is one of them. This is for two reasons. His family asks for forgiveness. It is also for the relationship between the two countries. Difficult words: hearing (a legal event), guilty (that he was a spy, that he did something illegal), government (the ‘bosses’ of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Karachi, Pakistan, an attack happened at the Chinese consulate , killing two police officers and two civilians who were collecting Chinese visas . There is a video of the attack but it is unclear whether the people filmed are the attackers or the security services arriving in response. The Balochistan Liberation Army, a separatist group, claimed responsibility for the attack because it does not want China in Pakistan. It calls China an ‘ oppressor ’. Difficult words: consulate (a building used for diplomacy – talks among countries), visa (special permission on a passport that says a person can enter, leave or stay for a certain time in a country), liberation (freedom), separatist (breakaway), oppressor (a country which makes other countries do what they want them to do). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Karachi, Pakistan a separatist group claimed responsibility for an attack at a Chinese government building because it does not want China in Pakistan. It calls China an ‘ oppressor ’. The attack killed two police officers and two civilians who were collecting paperwork for Chinese people in Pakistan. It is unclear who the people are in the video of the attack. It could be either the attackers or security guards. Difficult words: separatist (a person or people who do not want to be a part of a larger group), claim responsibility (admit that you did something), oppressor (a country which makes other countries do what they want them to do), civilian (an ordinary person who is not a part of the military or the police). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Karachi, Pakistan a separatist group attacks a Chinese government building. It says that China is an ‘ oppressor ’. It does not want China in Pakistan. The attack kills two officers and two civilians . There is a video of the attack. We are not sure who the people are in the video. The people could be the attackers. They could also be guards coming to the attack. Difficult words: separatist group (a group which does not want to be a part of a bigger group), oppressor (a country which makes other countries do what they want them to do), civilian (a person who is not a part of the military or the police). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In central Italy in the town of San Felice Circeo, a huge sinkhole swallowed up a car after heavy rainfall in the region. No bodies have been found. Difficult words: huge (very big), swallow up (take in, let fall into). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

After heavy rainfall, a huge sinkhole opened up in a town in central Italy, and swallowed a car. No bodies were found. Difficult words: huge (very big), sinkhole (when water makes a space in the ground that comes up to the top of the ground), swallow up (take in, let fall into). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It rains heavily in central Italy. A sinkhole appears . A car falls into it. People do not find anyone dead. Difficult words: sinkhole (when water makes a hole in the ground that comes up to the top of the ground), appear (start to exist). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Moped thieves have long been the scourge of London’s pedestrians and motorists – they move fast and hope that the police will not engage in a potentially dangerous chase. The Metropolitan Police in London, however, have instructed the officers to assess the dangers of each situation individually and ram the thieves. Police released dash cam footage showing the tougher tactics against the criminals. Difficult words: scourge (something which causes great trouble), pedestrian (a person who is walking), assess (judge, think about), ram (hit), dash cam (a camera on the dashboard – the area in the car in front of the driver), footage (a video). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

One of London’s problems is its moped thieves, as they move fast and hope that police cannot chase them because it would be dangerous. However, London’s officers are employing a tougher method – they ram the thieves. Videos on the Internet show this in action. Difficult words: chase (move quickly after somebody to catch him or her), employ (make use of; do), ram (hit). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thieves on mopeds are a problem in London. They move fast. Chasing them can be dangerous. However, police are getting tougher with them. They hit them with their cars. Difficult words: thief (a person who takes somebody’s things), chasing (moving quickly after somebody to catch him or her), tough (hard, strict, not nice). Sentinelese tribes people killed American tourist John Allen Chau after he visited them. They live on the isolated Sentinel Island in the Bay of Bengal between India and Myanmar. India controls the territory and an Indian anthropology professor said that the tourist would have known if he had talked to other people that this tribe was aggressive. They shoot arrows and throw spears and getting too close to them is dangerous. The tribe is hostile to outsiders and is not immune to common infections like the flu , which is why Indian law restricts access to the island. Difficult words: tribes people (people belonging to a tribe – a smaller traditional society), hostile (aggressive), flu (influenza – a viral infection). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An American tourist died on an island between India and Myanmar. The Sentinelese tribes people who live there are known to be hostile to outsiders. India controls the territory of the island. An Indian anthropology professor talked about the tribe: they shoot arrows, and they throw spears if somebody gets too close. Common sicknesses can make them sick or kill them, so people cannot visit this island easily. Difficult words: tribes people (people who belong to a tribe – a smaller traditional society), hostile (aggressive), anthropology (the study of human societies and cultures). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from the Sentinelese island. It is between India and Myanmar. It is isolated . The people there are the Sentinelese. They are isolated. This makes them afraid of outsiders. They are aggressive . Also, they are not used to our sicknesses. An outsider can make them sick easily. This is why people cannot simply visit this island. India controls this. However, an American tourist goes there. The Sentinelese kill him. Difficult words: isolated (when a place or a people are far away from other places or people), aggressive (violent and ready to fight), outsider (a person who is not part of a group).
